Plan: Signal Hound BB60 as a wvt live device¶

Issue: #2. Branch: 2-signal-hound (from main; the first version was on wvt-sh-dev, commit 72f9d8a). Status: implemented on 2-signal-hound (2026-10-20) against bb_api 5.0.11 (SDK 2026-10-05), tested with a simulated BB60 (section 7). Not yet run against hardware. Sections 1 to 6 are the first plan and its review; section 7 records the second pass.

1. Goal¶

Add the Signal Hound BB60D (and BB60C / BB60A) to the hardware device options, next to RTL-SDR and USRP B2xx. The user can select it in the Device list or with --device bb, tune it, set its reference level, view the spectrum and waterfall, and record SigMF or raw IQ.

Out of scope: BB60 sweep mode, triggers / GPS time stamps, the SM200/SM435 or other Signal Hound devices, transmit.

2. Design decisions¶

Topic

Decision

Reason

API

bb_api from the Signal Hound SDK, linked as an imported shared library

No distro package or pkg-config file exists

Build switch

WVT_WITH_BB = AUTO / ON / OFF, SIGNALHOUND_SDK_DIR hint

Same pattern as WVT_WITH_RTLSDR / WVT_WITH_UHD

Driver id

"bb", device args = serial number

Short, matches rtlsdr / uhd naming

Sample format

bbDataType16sc → SampleFormat::CI16

Half the bandwidth of cf32; recorder and ring already handle ci16 (USRP)

Sample rate

40 MS/s / 2^n, n = 0..13 (40 MS/s .. 4.883 kS/s), shown as a combo, requests snapped on a log scale

The BB60 only decimates by powers of 2

“Gain”

Reused StreamConfig::gain as reference level in dBm (-130 .. +20); GainRange gets label / unit

The BB60 has no gain control; ref level picks atten/amp

Manual RF

atten (-1 auto, 0-3 → 0/10/20/30 dB) and rfGain (-1 auto, 0-3)

Expose bbConfigureGainAtten

Bandwidth

StreamConfig::bandwidth reused as the I/Q filter bandwidth; 0 = widest for the rate

Same field the USRP uses

External ref

extRef → bbConfigureIO port 1 = 10 MHz in

Lab use

Retune / ref-level change

Stop thread → bbAbort → configure → bbInitiate → restart thread with purge

The BB60 applies settings only at bbInitiate

Retune gap

Not reported as a gap; the recorder starts a new SigMF capture segment and the purge drops old samples

Matches how retunes already work for the other drivers

3. Work breakdown (as implemented)¶

Phase 1 — Build system (CMakeLists.txt)¶

  • [x] WVT_WITH_BB, SIGNALHOUND_SDK_DIR cache variables.

  • [x] find_path(bb_api.h) with SDK sub-folder suffixes; find_library(bb_api).

  • [x] Fallback glob for the versioned libbb_api.so.5.0.x, choosing x86-64 vs aarch64 from CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR, skipping symlinks.

  • [x] Imported target bb_api, adds src/device/sdr_bb60.cpp, defines WVT_HAVE_BB.

  • [x] ON fails hard when not found; AUTO prints a status line.

Phase 2 — Device abstraction (src/device/sdr_device.h/.cpp)¶

  • [x] StreamConfig: atten, rfGain, extRef; comments for bb use of args, gain, bandwidth.

  • [x] GainRange: label, unit.

  • [x] sdrDrivers(), enumerateDevices() (with a “none detected” placeholder), openDevice() dispatch.

  • [x] checkSampleRate("bb"): range check + warning above 10 MS/s (host-side filtering).

  • [x] New supportedRates(driver) and snapSampleRate(driver, rate).

Phase 3 — Backend (src/device/sdr_bb60.cpp, new)¶

  • [x] Open by first device or by serial; read device type and serial for the description.

  • [x] Configure: ext ref (BB60D vs BB60C port constants), 16-bit I/Q, center, ref level, gain/atten, decimation + bandwidth (clamped to the per-decimation maximum).

  • [x] Streaming thread: bbGetIQUnpacked in ~20 ms blocks (1 k – 256 k samples), purge on (re)start, sample-loss → gap_(-1, …), bbADCOverflow → “ADC overload” note for 1 s, bbDeviceConnectionErr → fatal error.

  • [x] reconfigure() restarts the stream for retune / ref level and rolls back on failure.

  • [x] Reads back the actual rate with bbQueryIQParameters.

  • [x] enumerateBb() via bbGetSerialNumberList2.

Phase 4 — CLI (src/app/main.cpp)¶

  • [x] --device bb[:SERIAL], --ref-level DBM, --atten auto|0|10|20|30, --bb-amp auto|0-3 (first --amp, which the generator amplitude option already used; renamed in #54), --ext-ref.

  • [x] Default rate 10 MS/s and ref level -20 dBm for bb when not given.

  • [x] Help text updates.

Phase 5 — GUI (src/app/app_live.cpp)¶

  • [x] Driver name “BB60”, default gain range as ref level.

  • [x] Rate combo for drivers with discrete rates.

  • [x] Gain slider uses GainRange::label/unit; for BB60 the value applies on slider release (each change restarts the stream).

  • [x] Reset gain to a meaningful default when switching to / from bb.

  • [x] BB60 toolbar row: Atten, Amp, Bandwidth, Ext ref (each restarts the stream).

Phase 6 — Docs (README.md)¶

  • [x] Build instructions for the SDK, udev / USB 3 / Spike notes, device table column, CLI options, ref-level behavior, source-file table.

4. Review findings (to fix or verify)¶

Ordered by expected impact.

  1. Platform support is not stated. The Signal Hound SDK ships bb_api for Windows and Linux (x86-64, aarch64) only. wvt builds on Linux and macOS (XQuartz), so on macOS BB60 support is always off, and the CMake glob only searches .so*. README should say “Linux only” in the BB60 build section and the device table.

  2. Device re-scan while a BB60 streams. bbGetSerialNumberList2 may not list a device that is already open. Then App::scanDevices() sees found == false and calls selectDevice(devices_.front()), which changes devCfg_ while the BB60 still streams. Verify on hardware; if it happens, keep the open device in the list (add it from liveStats_ when streaming) or skip re-selection while running.

  3. Max I/Q bandwidth table is approximate. maxBandwidth() uses 0.8 × rate for decimation ≥ 4. Check against the SDK manual’s table for bbConfigureIQ (some decimations allow less than 80%). If the API rejects the value, open fails with a generic error; clamp to the documented table instead.

  4. Retune marker timing relies on the first block taking ~20 ms. LiveEngine::setCenterFreq sets freshFrom_ and calls rec_.noteRetune() after dev_->setCenterFreq() returns, but the BB60 thread already restarted inside that call. The comment in reconfigure() assumes ~20 ms, but the block size is clamped to 262 144 samples, so the first block takes only ~6.5 ms at 40 MS/s and ~13 ms at 20 MS/s (plus bbInitiate latency). At low rates it is safe (1024 samples ≈ 210 ms at 4.88 kS/s). A more robust option: let the backend mark the boundary itself (e.g. a callback, or start the thread only after the engine records the marker).

  5. UI stall on retune. setCenterFreq / setGain run on the UI thread and do join + bbAbort + bbInitiate. Measure; if > ~100 ms, move reconfigure to the device thread or debounce frequency edits.

  6. External reference on BB60A. The code uses the BB60C port-1 constant for any non-D device. Confirm the BB60A accepts it, or disable Ext ref for the BB60A.

  7. setGain compares refLevel_ without cfgM_. Harmless today (UI thread only), but take the lock for consistency with reconfigure().

  8. Style: in src/app/main.cpp the --ext-ref branch shares a line with --antenna (... dev.extRef = true; else if (a == "--antenna") ...). Split it to match the surrounding one-option-per-branch layout.

  9. --gain auto with --device bb sets agc = true, which the BB60 ignores. Either reject it with a message (“BB60: use –ref-level”) or document it.

5.2 Build verification¶

  • [ ] Linux x86-64: build with -DSIGNALHOUND_SDK_DIR=… straight from the SDK folder (versioned .so only) and with the library installed in /usr/local/lib.

  • [ ] Linux aarch64 (e.g. Raspberry Pi 5 / Jetson): confirm the glob picks the ARM library.

  • [ ] WVT_WITH_BB=ON without the SDK: CMake fails with the expected message.

  • [ ] WVT_WITH_BB=AUTO without the SDK (incl. macOS): builds, --device bb gives “built without bb support”.

7. Second pass (2026-10-20)¶

The first version (72f9d8a) was ported to the current main and checked against the SDK of 2026-10-05 (bb_api 5.0.12 for Linux ARM64, 5.0.11 for macOS ARM, 5.0.9 for Linux x86-64).

7.1 Review findings: outcome¶

#

Finding

Outcome

1

Platform support

The SDK now has a macOS ARM library (5.0.11). CMake finds the .dylib, copies it to build/bb_api/ with an @rpath install name, and refuses an x86-64 macOS build with a clear reason. The macOS library decimates by 128 at most, so the rate list on macOS stops at 312.5 kS/s. It needs libusb from the ARM Homebrew at run time

2

Rescan while streaming

scanDevices no longer changes the selection while a device streams. The device box shows the description of the streaming device, because an open BB60 is not listed

3

Bandwidth table

Replaced with the manual’s table (bbMaxBandwidth): 27, 17.8, 8, 3.75, 2, 1 MHz, 500, 250, 140, 65, 30, 15, 8, 4 kHz

4

Retune marker timing

Fixed: SdrDevice::setRetuneMark / usesRetuneMark. The BB60 calls the mark after its thread stopped and before the new stream starts, so the capture segment starts at the first new sample. bb_check verifies it on both sides of each boundary

5

UI stall on retune

The restart time is logged (DEBUG retune applied in N ms). To measure on hardware

6

Ext ref on the BB60A

The BB60A and BB60C share the port 1 constants (header documentation); kept

7

setGain lock

Fixed

8

--ext-ref style

Fixed

9

--gain auto with the BB60

Refused: “the BB60 has no automatic gain: use –ref-level DBM”

7.2 Other changes¶

  • Linux x86-64: the SDK has a folder for each distribution. CMake takes the newest version 5 library and skips Ubuntu 14.04 (the old version 3 API). It copies libftd2xx.so next to it and links it, so the loader finds it through wvt’s rpath. It makes the libbb_api.so.5 and libbb_api.so links that the loader needs.

  • file(COPY_FILE) (CMake 3.21) is not used, because the minimum is CMake 3.16.

  • Open-time notes (a snapped rate, a limited bandwidth) show before the stream starts.

  • Logging: [bb] component (open, configure, stream start time, restart time, errors).

7.3 Simulated BB60¶

tools/bb_sim/ has a header with the part of bb_api.h that wvt uses (the same declarations and values as 5.0.x) and a simulated BB60D (serial 12345678). It checks the arguments as the manual documents them (power-of-2 decimation, the bandwidth table, frequency range), streams in real time, and makes a 100.2 MHz, −30 dBm tone with noise. It returns bbADCOverflow when the tone is above the reference level. WVT_BB_SIM_NONE=1 hides the device and WVT_BB_SIM_UNPLUG=S disconnects it after S seconds. -DWVT_BB_SIM=ON builds wvt and bb_check with it; the Linux CI job uses it.
